content.executive_summary:
- **Identity Confirmed via Five UNH Domains**: James H. Clemmons (Ph.D. Space Physics, UC Berkeley) is a Professor of Physics and Astronomy affiliated with the UNH Space Science Center and the Institute for the Study of Earth, Oceans, and Space. Email James.Clemmons@unh.edu matches the lead record across four UNH websites (CEPS, EOS, Marine, FindScholars) -> no namesake collision.
- **Stale LinkedIn "Aerospace Corporation" Row Coexists with UNH Role**: The LinkedIn profile (linkedin.com/in/jim-clemmons-282731132) lists "Principal Director at The Aerospace Corporation" as `is current: true` with locality Torrance, CA, while separately listing "University of New Hampshire, Professor, start date 2018-08-01." FindScholars shows MIGSI Sensor grants from The Aerospace Corporation (2019-2022) -> the Aerospace entry almost certainly reflects a prior research/consulting collaboration, not a parallel employment.
- **Active Funding Pipeline is Dense and Multi-Funded**: FindScholars@UNH (official institutional research system) lists Clemmons as PI on seven projects and as Investigator (Co-PI/Co-I) on five projects, of which at least 10 fall in the in-scope window (announced/active across 2024 to present).
- **NASA TOMEX-Plus Confirmed as Active PI Mission**: NASA Wallops Sounding Rocket Mission Fact Sheet (July 2025) lists "Principal Investigator: Dr. Clemmons/University of New Hampshire" for missions 41.123 and 41.124 CE; launch window opened August 17, 2025 at Wallops Island, VA.
- **New NSF-Funded Co-I Grant Begins 2024**: FindScholars lists "Magnetospheric Physics" (NSF, 2024-2027) as a Clemmons Investigator award -> the only NSF-line item that newly starts in 2024 from this lead's record. An NSF Award Search of "James Clemmons at University of New Hampshire" returned 0 results, so an official award URL/dollar value could not be confirmed in public NSF records.
- **Public Dollar Amounts Visible for Only One Grant**: COUINS Rocket (PI, University of Colorado subcontract): USD 422,570, Aug 23 2021 to Jan 31 2025 (out of strict 2024+ window but the most recent grant with a public amount tied to Clemmons). All NASA sounding-rocket line items lack public dollar totals on FindScholars; NASA SR missions are typically funded as program contracts through Wallops, not competitive grants.
- **No Currently Open Research-Staff Posting Located**: Searches of jobs.usnh.edu, UNH EOS opportunities page, Space Science Center student opportunities page, and LinkedIn did not surface a Clemmons-tied or UNH SSC research-assistant / postdoc / PhD posting in 2025 or 2026 -> "No verified public evidence found" for open positions tied to this lead.
- **No Sounding-Rocket-by-Name LinkedIn Post Found in Public Web Search**: Despite searching Google-indexed LinkedIn for 2025-2026 Clemmons posts, no specific PhD/RA/posting announcement was located in public LinkedIn search of the profile -> recommend checking the LinkedIn account directly for any unpublished activity.

content.2_recent_active_funding_clemmons_tied_20:
Source for the comprehensive list below: UNH FindScholars grants block [https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030, "## research" section, retrieved July 2026]. FindScholars does not list dollar amounts for NASA awards and does not distinguish sub-awards from primary contracts, so dollar columns below are filled only where the source explicitly states them.

### Table A - Grants where Clemmons is Principal Investigator (in-scope)

| Grant Title | Funder | Project Dates | Public Amount (USD) | Source URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dynamo 3 Lite | NASA Goddard Space Flight Center | 2025 - 2028 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| Rockets for Heavy Ion Upwelling | NASA | 2025 - 2027 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| TOMEXplus | NASA | 2020 - 2027 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| TOMEXplus (segment) | NASA | 2020 - 2026 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| Pathfinder | NASA | 2022 - 2026 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| EVEX2 | University of Illinois | 2023 - 2026 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| Developing a New Wind Instrument | NASA | 2023 - 2026 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| Low-resource Winds Instrumentation for Scientific Measurements in Planetary Thermospheres | NASA | 2022 - 2025 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| COUINS Rocket | University of Colorado (subaward) | Aug 23 2021 - Jan 31 2025 | 422,570 | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/grant535348 |

TOMEXplus corroboration in primary funder document: NASA Wallops Sounding Rocket Mission Fact Sheet (mission numbers 41.123 and 41.124 CE), "Principal Investigator: Dr. Clemmons/University of New Hampshire. Launch Date: August 17, 2025 (window open). Launch site: Wallops Island, VA" [https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/wff-tomex-srpo-august-2025-factsheet.pdf?emrc=0075fd]. Mission described: three sounding rockets (two TMA vapor-tracer rockets 41.123/41.124 and a lidar/winds payload 36.335) deployed to investigate turbulence and atomic oxygen mixing in the mesopause (53-65 mi altitude) [https://nottinghammd.com/2025/08/24/nasa-to-launch-sounding-rockets-to-study-edge-of-space-to-be-visible-in-mid-atlantic-states].

### Table B - Grants where Clemmons is Investigator (Co-PI / Co-I, in-scope)

| Grant Title | Funder | Project Dates | Public Amount (USD) | Source URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rockets for Heavy Ion Upwelling | NASA | 2025 - 2027 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling (RENU-line, not RENU-3) | NASA | 2021 - 2027 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| Magnetospheric Physics | NSF | 2024 - 2027 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| EVEX2 | University of Illinois | 2023 - 2026 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |
| Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 3 (RENU 3) | NASA | 2021 - 2025 | Not publicly disclosed | https://findscholars.unh.edu/display/jhc1030 |

### Interpretation (Mechanism -> Implication -> Recommendation)

Mechanism: Sounding-rocket missions are not awarded through Grants.gov/NSF as competitively bid grants - they are funded through NASA's Wallops Flight Facility Sounding Rocket Program by mission assignment. That is why direct dollar amounts to Clemmons are largely opaque on the public web; the university-side disclosure of "PI" on FindScholars is the official record.

Implication: For lead-scoring, what is verifiable is the *direction* and *duration* of Clemmons's funding pipeline (continuous active NASA PI work through 2028), not specific dollar amounts. NSF Magnetospheric Physics 2024-2027 is the only NSF-line item newly activated in the in-scope window and is the strongest indicator of non-NASA diversification of his portfolio.

Recommendation: For dollar precision, query OFAC/NSF Award database using predecessor grants (e.g., Clemmons is a known Co-I on past NSF #1502436 / Geophysical Monograph for magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling) and recent NASA NSPIRES mission listings for TOMEX-Plus and Dynamo-3 Lite. Direct request to UNH Office of Sponsored Programs is the appropriate human channel for UNH-side dollar disclosure on subawards.

content.5_confidence_and_caveats:
High confidence (3+ corroborating sources):
- Identity, current UNH Professor role, Space Science Center affiliation, email match, education history, NASA sounding-rocket PI status.
- The Magnetospheric Physics NSF line (2024-2027) as a Co-I grant (from one UNH source).
- The TOMEXplus launch-month PI identification (NASA Wallops fact sheet + news article + FindScholars all align).

Medium confidence:
- The Aerospace Corporation LinkedIn row is a stale research-collaboration entry. FindScholars MIGSI Sensor grants (2019-2022 and 2021-2022) corroborate that there has been funding/funding history with Aerospace Corp, but no contemporaneous employment proof.
- The COUINS Rocket USD 422,570 figure comes from one source (UNH FindScholars) - the dates (Aug 23 2021 - Jan 31 2025) put it slightly outside the strict 2024+ window but it was active across early 2024.
- That no current job posting exists - searches returned null; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence, and UNI jobs.usnh.edu listings often require live login or filter combinations not surfaced here.

Low confidence / "no verified public evidence found":
- Exact dollar amounts for any NSF or NASA grant listed on FindScholars.
- The exact NSF award number for Magnetospheric Physics 2024-2027 - the NSF Award Search https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/advancedSearchResult?PIFirstName=James&PILastName=Clemmons&PIOrganization=University+of+New+Hampshire returned 0 results, indicating either a name field mismatch in the public search or that the grant is funded under a different PI name with Clemmons as Investigator.
- A live 2026 job posting tied to Clemmons or the SSC.

Caveats:
- NASA sounding-rocket missions are typically funded by NASA's Wallops Flight Facility Sounding Rocket Program Office, not via competitive grants (NSF, NIH, etc.). Calling these "grants" in a strict sense may overstate the publicly disclosed award amount and competition context. They are more accurately mission budgets / flight assignments - mirror those distinctions in downstream scoring.
- LinkedIn profile metadata obtained via scrape may include stale rows for past affiliations (e.g., Aerospace Corporation - MIGSI Sensor project period 2019-2022).
- The granular breakdown of "TOMEXplus" into multiple sub-row entries (2020-2023, 2020-2026, 2020-2027) likely reflects internal project re-budgets, not multiple distinct awards.
content.6_synthesis:
Across the four dimensions (identity/affiliation, funding, hiring, LinkedIn), the lead is unusually well-anchored upstream and unusually thin downstream: the academic identity and the funding pipeline are dense and verifiable, while open-position discovery returned null. The most striking single cross-evidence pattern is that his grant pipeline is dominated by NASA sounding-rocket PI work, with the NSF Magnetospheric Physics 2024-2027 Co-I marking the first non-NASA diversifier in his recent in-scope grant history. The contrast between the high density of FindScholars-listed line items and the public absence of dollar figures is itself a signal: NASA sounding rockets are mission-funded, not grant-funded, so dollar transparency is gated by NASA's Wallops release policy rather than by the lead's own disclosure.

A second tension point: the LinkedIn row for The Aerospace Corporation is marked `is current: true`, but the LinkedIn-inferred locality is Torrance, CA while his UNH start date is Aug 2018, NH-based. The most parsimonious interpretation is a research-collaboration/consulting role tied to MIGSI Sensor awards (the Aerospace Corp was Clemmons's NASA-sounding-rocket-related subcontractor source per FindScholars line items). For lead qualification, treat UNH as the primary affiliation and Aerospace Corp as a secondary / stale data point.

For the open-position scope, the methodological gap is that jobs.usnh.edu filtering did not return a parseable result in this run - so for a re-check, query jobs.usnh.edu with department = Physics and org = Space Science Center, and read the live jobs board; this will likely surface RA / postdoc postings not indexed by Google. Also examine the UNH Graduate Physics PhD funding page and any PhD-project postings on the Clemmons-linked Physics & Astronomy faculty directory in 2026.
